metadata.title: Top clean energy stocks to watch as Democratic sweep improves outlook

content.text:
Investing.com -- The Democratic sweep has lifted clean energy, though the screen shows a sector that was badly beaten up first. Most names are still deeply negative over 3 months and 1 year despite today's pops. That sets up a rebound trade, not a sector already at highs. Screener figures are snapshots and may lag live prices.
The Screen (US Renewables, >$1B)
Names Worth Watching
-
Profitable and cheap: First Solar (FSLR) trades at a 10.1x forward P/E, the lowest among the profitable large caps here. Reuters noted it gained 9.4% on the election reaction. Read more (Nov 4, 2026)
-
Policy-sensitive residential solar: Sunrun Inc (RUN) and Enphase (ENPH) are down 54.5% and 31.7% (1Y and 3M). Their upside is largest if federal support holds, but they also have the most to lose if it doesn't.
-
Supply-chain angle: Nextpower (NXT) has the smallest drawdown of the large names, at -11.7% over 3 months. Its 5.4% move today suggests it is already catching a bid.
-
Fuel cells: Bloom Energy rose about 6% pre-open after a Barclays upgrade and a carbon-capture partnership. Read more (Nov 4, 2026) It didn't appear in this screen, so its metrics have not been checked.
Risks to the Thesis
-
Speculative names: Plug Power (PLUG) was up 8.5% pre-open on a high beta of over 2, with earnings due November 9. Read more Negative forward earnings at Fluence Energy (FLNC) and SolarEdge (SEDG) make them momentum plays.
-
Limited power: The result is a divided government, and the Reuters piece says Democrats may lack the numbers to pass major legislation. Gains could fade if "reinforced support" means only fewer rollbacks and no new incentives.
-
Chasing the gap: Many names rose 5–9% today after steep declines, so some of the relief may already be priced in.
Overall, the profitable, lower-multiple names have the clearest fundamental cushion. The deeply beaten, loss-making ones offer more upside and more risk.
